text:
incident-bot: PAGED -> pagerduty: INC-17077 — service=runtime-hotpath | symptom=p99 latency spike > 1200ms | SLO burn 3m
incident-bot: link: https://pagerduty.company/INC-17077 | auto-escalation in 5m if unacked

samir: acked. I'm on it. looking at hotpath fleet and router fanout

elaine: customer-facing note: a few enterprise customers reported timeouts in dashboards ~5m ago, low % of requests but obvious tail impact

kevin: quick ask — is this kv-cache eviction or routing amplification? any hotkeys?

samir: initial look: no obvious hotkey spike. backend error rates ok. saw bursty queue length on sidecar pods serving gpt-medium-8k variant. p99 token latency jumped first.

nina: routing: fallback policy to cheaper model should have engaged but logs show failure to flip for ~90s. investigating router agent logs

samir: attempting temporary mitigation: will scale up dedicated hotpath pool and reduce batch size to cut tail. running:
```sh
# scale runtime hotpath pool
kubectl -n runtime scale deployment/hotpath-pool --replicas=6
# reduce global batch size (safemode)
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/config -d '{"hotpath.batch_max_tokens": 32}'
```

kevin: if scaling doesn't hold, we should route 10% of traffic to fallback region and engage canary rollback for the latest routing change from today at 09:12 UTC

samir: scale applied. batch size updated. router-agent logs show an error when applying fallback flag: "timeout applying policy to 3/10 agents" — pushing a retry

nina: retry succeeded on the remaining agents. fallback policy now active for 15% traffic. monitoring p95/p99

samir: p95 back to ~280ms, p99 down from 1850ms -> 520ms within 60s after fallback. keeping oncall watch for 10min to ensure stability :thumbsup:

elaine: noted customer impact for postmortem: "transient dashboard timeouts for subset of enterprise customers, mitigated by routing fallback and scale-up; no data loss." I'll patch into incident doc and notify cs for outbound blurb later

kevin: looks like the root cause is a routing agent race on policy propagation — filing infra-ticket INFRA-17077 and tagging runtime-team

samir: agreed. I'll hand off to infra on next shift. I'll add timeline and commands used to the incident doc. closing page in PD and switching thread to monitoring. thanks all.

incident-bot: PD INC-17077 status: acknowledged -> resolved by samir at 1707700120.

samir: follow-ups: create a canary for router policy propagation and add alert for policy-apply latency > 30s.
